cards.name: Gloom
cards.notes: Gloom from Unbroken Bonds 7/214 is included in this guide as a sleepy Pokemon card for collectors building a calm, cozy, or nap-themed binder. As an uncommon card, it is useful for collectors who want the sleepy theme to feel complete beyond only the expensive hits. The card is illustrated by Anesaki Dynamic, which is useful context for collectors who like arranging pages by artist as well as by Pokemon. Its low market price makes it one of the easiest sleepy Pokemon cards to add to a binder without stretching a collection budget. It can help bridge older modern sets with newer illustration rares in a mixed-era sleepy Pokemon layout.
cards.whyItBelongs: Out cold drooling on a garden path. Anesaki Dynamic gives Gloom an unapologetically messy outdoor nap complete with drool puddles.

cards.name: Tangrowth
cards.notes: Tangrowth rests quietly among the greenery.
cards.whyItBelongs: Tangrowth is settled at the base of a big tree with its eyes gently shut, one red hand tucked up near its face. Sunlight filters through the leaves behind it, ferns crowd in at the edges, and a tiny curled sprout pokes up in front like it’s keeping watch. There’s no battle pose and no drama here, just a very large, very tangled Pokémon getting some rest in the shade.

cards.name: Espurr
cards.notes: Espurr has nodded off in the grass beneath a shady tree.
cards.whyItBelongs: Espurr is stretched out in the grass beneath a broad tree, eyes closed and mouth open in a tiny sleepy yawn. HYOGONOSUKE's sun-dappled scene makes this feel like a warm afternoon nap interrupted only by the light.

cards.name: Wigglytuff
cards.notes: Wigglytuff from Unbroken Bonds 135/214 is included in this guide as a sleepy Pokemon card for collectors building a calm, cozy, or nap-themed binder. As a rare card, it gives the sleepy Pokemon theme a little more collector weight without necessarily becoming the whole page. The card is illustrated by miki kudo, which is useful context for collectors who like arranging pages by artist as well as by Pokemon. Its approachable market price makes it a strong budget pick for building out a sleepy Pokemon binder page. It can help bridge older modern sets with newer illustration rares in a mixed-era sleepy Pokemon layout.
cards.whyItBelongs: Two Jigglypuff have completely dozed off beside an enormous, happily awake Wigglytuff in a sunny meadow. Wigglytuff’s Pokédex lore repeatedly describes its fine, luxurious fur as irresistibly comfortable to cuddle, even noting that sleeping while holding one feels wonderful. Add an attack called Sleepy Ball, and Wigglytuff is basically functioning as the world’s fluffiest communal nap pillow.

cards.name: Snorlax
cards.notes: Community submission. Snorlax is dozing beneath a tree while Pikachu keep him company.
cards.whyItBelongs: A full-on Snorlax nap under the trees, with two Pikachu nearby and a Torchic perched on his head. Nobody in this scene looks in a hurry to wake him.
